newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea posts record monthly deficit.
newsitem.headline: South Korea posts record monthly deficit.

text.p: South Korea posted a monthly record trade deficit of $2.9 billion in August, the result of falling semiconducter prices and brisk domestic consumption, the trade ministry said on Monday.
Shaken by a slew of discouraging trade data, Finance Minister Han Seung-woo will outline new economic policies on Tuesday, a ministry spokesman said.
Han was appointed to his post in August in a partial cabinet reshuffle, replacing Rha Woong-bae who was criticised for not doing enough to bring the ballooning current account deficit under control.
Han is expected to announce the new policies in a news conference at 2.30 pm (0530 GMT), although economists said they did not believe he had much room for maneuver.

"I don't think the new package will be any different from the old one because the government has very little room for policy changes," said Tae Chung, head of research at Jardine Fleming Securities in Seoul.
"The problems that face the economy aren't ones that the government can fix through new policy."
Lee Jae-kil, a senior trade official, said the August deficit "is due largely to the semiconductor shock".
The customs-cleared deficit in August surpassed the previous monthly record shortfall of $2.74 billion in July and a deficit of $901 million a year earlier.
In the first eight months the deficit widened to $13.29 billion from $8.45 billion a year earlier.
Exports totalled $9.95 billion in August, down 6.2 percent from $10.61 billion a year earlier, while imports were $12.86 billion, up 11.7 percent from $11.52 billion.
The steady increase in imports was attributed mostly to a 30.3 percent year-on-year growth in imports of consumer goods.

Trade officials, embarrassed by the worse-than-expected figures, declined to make any new prediction on the deficit for the whole of this year. Their latest prediction, made two months ago, was $11 billion.
Last year's deficit was $10 billion. Private economists said it could double this year to $20 billion, slightly more than four percent of projected gross domestic product.
"If price conditions don't improve, the shortfall would reach $20 billion this year," said Kim Chul-hoi, an economist at Dongwon Economic Research Institute.
The trade ministry's Lee said semiconducter exports, projected earlier at $30.7 billion for the whole of 1996, would be cut by $12.7 billion to $18 billion.
Exports of semiconductors, which account for about 20 percent of South Korea's total exports, fell 52 percent in value terms to $1.02 billion in August.

Spot prices for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips fell 78 percent to $12 in August from a year ago. Semiconductor exports for the January-August period were down 4.2 percent to $12.44 billion this year from $12.99 billion a year ago.

Exports of all other items in the eight months rose a combined 9.6 percent to $72.73 billion from $66.36 billion. In the first 20 days of August, exports of steel products fell by 10.1 percent, while those of petrochemical products dropped 10.6 percent, hit by a weak Japanese yen.
